item.title: George Clinton Sues Universal Music Over Alleged Royalty Freeze: ‘Financially Crippling’
item.description:
[Music fades out, and the host begins speaking]
Host: "Welcome back to 'The Beat'. Today, we're talking about a legendary musician who's taking on a music giant. George Clinton, the iconic founder of Parliament-Funkadelic, is suing Universal Music Group over a dispute that's left him financially strapped. Let's dive in.
George Clinton is accusing UMG of 'financially crippling' him by freezing over $1 million in royalty accounts. This all stems from a long-standing dispute over ownership of his catalog. But here's the twist: the lawsuit that started it all, filed by the estate of late Parliament-Funkadelic member Bernie Worrell, was dismissed last year.
Despite this, UMG is still refusing to pay Clinton his royalties. His lawyers claim that UMG is withholding 100% of royalties from Clinton, even though the Worrell lawsuit only dealt with a 50% cut. And with UMG no longer a party to the case, Clinton's team argues that there's no longer any legal justification for the freeze.
This isn't Clinton's first rodeo when it comes to litigation. He's fought battles with Worrell's estate and his former agent, Armen Boladian. But this case is particularly striking, given the amount of money at stake and the fact that UMG is still withholding royalties despite the dismissal of the Worrell lawsuit.
We've reached out to UMG for comment, but so far, no response. Clinton's lawsuit is a clear call to action: he wants his royalties, and he wants them now. We'll be keeping an eye on this case as it unfolds. That's all for today. Thanks for tuning in to 'The Beat'."
[Music fades back in]
